observations: Multiple electronic keyboards wrapped in clear plastic film.
The keyboards vary in key count: one appears to have 49 keys, another 61 keys, and a third 88 keys.
The control panels are visible but the brand names are not legible in the photos.
The items are displayed on a tiled floor in what appears to be a shop or warehouse.
A watermark 'MARY OLUGBAMI POSTED ON JIJI' is present on all images.

claims.evidence: The plastic wrapping obscures the surface condition and prevents testing of the internal electronics.
The seller's price is not provided in the text.

risks.risk: The keyboards may be non-functional or have dead keys.
risks.proof: A video showing each keyboard powered on and playing a scale across all keys.

risks.risk: The key count may be lower than the seller's description.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the key count sticker on the back of the keyboard.
risks.if_unproven: as the lowest key count model (49 keys)

risks.risk: The plastic wrapping may conceal scratches, dents, or cracks on the casing.
risks.proof: Photos of the keyboards with the plastic film removed.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Video of each keyboard being played to confirm all keys and buttons work.
Photo of the key count sticker on the back of the keyboard.
Photos of the keyboards without the plastic wrapping.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
